title: Argenx to buy peptide platform in potentially billion-dollar deal
content: An article from Dive Brief Argenx to buy peptide platform in potentially billion-dollar deal For $550 million up front, Argenx will take control of Unnatural Products’ “macrocyclic peptide” technology and direct it to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. Published Nov. 9, 2026 Jacob Bell Lead Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Argenx agreed to acquire Unnatural Products, a maker of "macrocyclic peptides," on Nov. 9, 2026. deliormanli via Getty Images Dive Brief: Argenx, a Netherlands-based biotechnology company focused on antibody drugs, on Monday said it has agreed to acquire a protein specialist in a potentially billion-dollar-plus deal. Unnatural Products has a platform that pairs machine learning, screening and other techniques to engineer “macrocyclic peptides.” These peptides are larger and more complex than typical small molecules, which allows them to more effectively bind to tricky proteins and address some challenging diseases. Yet, they’re still tiny enough that they can be swallowed. Argenx plans to use the platform to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. The acquisition carries a $550 million upfront cash payment. Unnatural Products could receive up to $595 million more if specific milestones are hit. if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Dive Insight: Unnatural Products claims macrocyclic peptides hold the potential to unlock targets once thought to be “undruggable.” That premise, along with the California company’s technology platform, proved enticing to both venture capitalists and big-name pharmaceutical firms like Merck & Co. and Novartis. Argenx was drawn in as well, having already taken a minority stake in Unnatural Products before pursuing a full buyout. In a statement, Argenx CEO Karen Massey said these macrocyclic peptide capabilities are “highly complementary” to her own company’s antibody engineering. “After working together for more than two years, we also know there is a strong fit in how we work: science first, entrepreneurial and focused on patients,” Massey added. “We want to preserve what has made [Unnatural Products] successful while bringing the strengths of both teams together.” The Food and Drug Administration has already approved at least a handful of macrocyclic peptide therapies. In 2020, for example, Rhythm Pharmaceuticals’ Imcivree was cleared as a treatment for certain genetic forms of obesity. The following year, Aurinia Pharmaceuticals’ Lupkynis became the first-ever oral medicine for adults with active lupus nephritis. In 2023, the FDA greenlit a UCB medicine called Zilbrysq for “generalized myasthenia gravis,” a rare autoimmune condition that’s become somewhat of a battleground for several developers. Argenx’s own flagship product, Vyvgart, targets this disease and brought in $4.5 billion in net product sales from January through the end of September. Thomas Smith, a Leerink Partners analyst who covers Argenx, wrote in a note to clients that the new acquisition “represents potential for longer-term strategic value.” He explained there’s a desire — both in big pharma and in the broader immunology and inflammation research space — to make oral, long-acting therapeutics that are able to be more effective and convenient than conventional biologics. The Unnatural Products deal, which comes on the heels of Argenx’s potentially $2.2 billion purchase of Forte Biosciences, also “signals further focus on pipeline growth and diversification,” Smith wrote. Shares of Argenx were up nearly 3% by late Monday morning, to hover around $953 apiece. Add us on Google Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Filed Under: Deals

title: Pfizer and Blackstone Sign Co-Funding Deal for berobenatide
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 12, 2026 Pfizer and Blackstone Sign Co-Funding Deal for berobenatide Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Pfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences sign a co-funding deal in which Blackstone is set to provide up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to advance berobenatide. Advertisement Pfizer Inc. and Blackstone Life Sciences entered a strategic co-funding agreement under which funds managed by Blackstone will pay upwards of $1.5 billion in development costs through 2028 for berobenatide.The investigational, potential first-in-class monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide is currently being studied for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions. In exchange for the funding, Blackstone will be eligible to receive milestone-based payments, subject to U.S. regulatory approval of monthly dosing of injectable berobenatide monotherapy for chronic weight management and the achievement of certain commercial sales milestones.1Cecile Guegan, chief financial officer and executive vice president, Pfizer, frames the agreement as part of a broader financing strategy for the company’s pipeline. “Our aim is to bring important new medicines to patients while taking a disciplined approach that pairs internal research investments with targeted investment from capital partners,” Guegan says. “Today’s announcement helps us advance our comprehensive obesity program and maintain the financial capacity and flexibility to invest in our broader pipeline across all therapeutic areas.”What are the terms of the agreement?Blackstone-managed funds are set to cover up to $1.5 billion of berobenatide’s development costs through 2028.1 In return, Blackstone becomes eligible for milestone-based payments tied to two conditions: U.S. regulatory approval of monthly dosing of injectable berobenatide monotherapy for chronic weight management, and the achievement of certain commercial sales milestones once the product reaches the market.1 The structure is expected to keep Blackstone purely as a capital partner rather than a stakeholder in the asset itself, as it holds no rights or ownership in berobenatide, while Pfizer continues to run the program’s operations and make its development decisions.1 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Related Articles FDA Requests Updated Safety Label Warning Across All GLP-1 Receptor Agonist for Potential Risk of NAION The US Drug-Pricing Reset: Competing on Net Value ESC 2026: GLP-1–Based Therapies Move Further into Mainstream Cardiovascular CareThe deal is expected to give Pfizer outside capital to fund one of the larger clinical programs in its pipeline without ceding control of the asset. Under terms of the agreement, Blackstone does not acquire any rights or ownership in berobenatide, while Pfizer retains full operational control and decision-making with respect to the berobenatide program.1 Any milestone payments, if earned, will be payable to Blackstone over a multi-year period, and funds managed by Blackstone’s perpetual private equity strategy, known as BXPE, will invest alongside funds managed by Blackstone Life Sciences as part of the transaction.1As Cheryl Reicin told Pharmaceutical Executive last year, with early-stage companies short on cash and big pharma short on new products, “options-to-buy have come back into vogue” as a way for large drugmakers to pursue multiple shots on goal in the GLP-1 class without loading R&D costs onto their own balance sheets.What is berobenatide and why does it matter for Pfizer’s pipeline?Berobenatide, is an investigational, potential first-in-class monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide being studied for chronic weight management and obesity-related comorbidities, including knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea.1,2 The drug is being studied across both weekly and monthly dosing intervals as part of the Vesper clinical program, which spans three trials.2 In Vesper-3, which tested a preplanned switch from weekly to monthly injections in adults without type 2 diabetes, berobenatide produced placebo-adjusted weight loss of up to 12.3% at 28 weeks, according to data presented by John B. Buse, MD, PhD, at the American Diabetes Association 2026 Scientific Sessions. Vesper-2 evaluated weekly dosing paired with glycemic improvement in adults who also had type 2 diabetes, while an open-label extension of Vesper-1 tested the drug at its highest weekly dose.2Pfizer is planning to advance more than 20 trials for obesity and related comorbidities in 2026, including 10 ongoing and planned Phase III trials for berobenatide.1Dr. Nicholas Galakatos, global head of Blackstone Life Sciences, points to the deal as a continuation of an existing relationship between the two organizations. “We are pleased to further expand our relationship with Pfizer and support the broad and rigorous development of berobenatide as the anchor of Pfizer’s cardiometabolic pipeline,” Galakatos says. “This collaboration is a good example of our leadership in providing capital solutions at scale to advance important medicines and technologies to patients.”SourcesPfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences Announce Strategic Funding Agreement for Obesity Program Pfizer November 11, 2026, https://www.pfizer.com/news/press-release/press-release-detail/pfizer-and-blackstone-life-sciences-announce-strategicBerobenatide weight loss benefit maintained in shift to monthly dosing, phase 2b data show Clevland Clinic Journal Of Medicine June 6, 2026, https://www.ccjm.org/page/ada-2026/berobenatide-monthly Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. title: AstraZeneca buys vaccine startup; FDA issues GLP-1 safety warning
content: An article from News roundup AstraZeneca buys vaccine startup; FDA issues GLP-1 safety warning The deal gives AstraZeneca a simpler way to make conjugate vaccines. Elsewhere, a psychedelic depression drug was submitted to the FDA and an autoimmune disease-focused biotech’s shares collapsed. Published Nov. 11, 2026 By BioPharma Dive staff Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving AstraZeneca and the Food and Drug Administration, as well as updates from Compass Pathways, Zura Bio and Abeona Therapeutics that you may have missed. AstraZeneca has acquired vaccine startup and development partner Omniose. The two companies didn't disclose deal terms in their announcement Tuesday. But the transaction hands AstraZeneca "bioconjugation" technology, a more efficient way to make the conjugate vaccines that strap a protein to an immune system-provoking antigen. Omniose claimed the technology could yield "higher-quality" conjugate vaccines. AstraZeneca intends to use the approach to make shots for serious bacterial infections. if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); The Food and Drug Administration has called for the prescribing information for widely popular GLP-1 therapies to be updated to include the possible risk of contracting a rare condition that causes vision loss. The FDA began investigating the issue following case reports of GLP-1 recipients developing "non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy," or "NAION." A review of animal data failed to uncover why GLP-1 drugs might be associated with NAION, but a meta-analysis of many trials found a higher rate of cases in treatment recipients. NAION's been seen with every marketed GLP-1 drug, too, the FDA said. The agency, as a result, believes there is a “potential increased risk of rare NAION events,” it said Monday. — Ben Fidler Compass Pathways said Monday it has completed an approval application in the U.S. for a synthetic psilocybin drug it calls “COMP360” and that it’s developed for treatment-resistant depression. In clinical testing, six weeks of treatment with COMP360 was associated with, on average, a 3.8-point reduction on a 60-point scale measuring the severity of depression symptoms. The drug is part of a wave of research into psychedelic medicines and could receive a particularly speedy review following the company’s receipt of a special Food and Drug Administration voucher. — Jonathan Gardner Shares of Zura Bio plunged by more than two-thirds on Monday following the company’s announcement that its lead product missed the main goal of a Phase 2 trial in people with the autoimmune skin condition hidradenitis suppurativa. Neither of two tested doses of the dual-pronged antibody drug tibulizumab significantly reduced the number of abscesses and inflammatory nodules in enrollees after 16 weeks, nor were secondary trial goals met. Zura will halt development in hidradenitis suppurativa, but continue studying tibulizumab in other immune diseases. title: 从强生获批到海思科III期：口服IL-23环肽赛道持续升温，HSK47388锚定银屑病治疗新路径
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 赛道梳理 从强生获批到海思科III期：口服IL-23环肽赛道持续升温，HSK47388锚定银屑病治疗新路径 从强生获批到海思科III期：口服IL-23环肽赛道持续升温，HSK47388锚定银屑病治疗新路径 周凯 · 产业与市场分析师 周 周凯 产业与市场分析师 审核：孙浩 · 特许金融分析师（CFA） 聚焦医药市场规模、产业链与竞争格局研究；长期跟踪院内销售数据、企业经营表现与重点赛道变化。累计发布市场分析报告 150+ 篇。 19小时前 1007 口服肽类药物 海思科医药集团股份有限公司 HSK47388片(I) IL-23 III期临床试验 口服环肽类药物研发持续升温，跨国药企加速布局，国内创新药项目也迎来新进展。11月11日，药物临床试验登记与信息公示平台显示，海思科自主研发的 HSK47388片(I) 针对中重度斑块状银屑病的III期临床试验启动，这是该药首次进入III期临床阶段。图源：药物临床试验登记与信息公示平台从海外药物获批到国内项目获得跨国药企青睐，口服肽类药物正成为全球创新药研发与BD交易的重要方向。一、MNC接连布局，口服肽类药物BD升温今年以来，全球口服肽类药物领域接连迎来重要进展。3月，强生的icotrokinra获FDA批准，成为全球首款获批上市的口服IL-23受体拮抗剂肽类药物，用于中重度斑块状银屑病治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库7月，默沙东的口服大环肽PCSK9抑制剂enlicitide获FDA批准，进一步拓展了口服肽类药物的应用领域。BD交易方面，国内相关项目也受到跨国药企关注。7月，翰森制药将口服IL-23受体拮抗剂HS-20118在大中华区以外地区的独家权益授权给Avere，交易总金额最高可达23亿美元，包括1.2亿美元首付款、最高21.8亿美元里程碑付款及销售提成。此前披露的早期临床数据显示，该药半衰期约100小时，具有潜在每周一次口服给药的可能性。图源：翰森制药企业公告10月，吉利德宣布以12.75亿美元现金首付款收购瀚辰星泰口服环状多肽IL-23R抑制剂HCXT-2001。该项目目前处于I期临床阶段，主要探索炎症性肠病等领域的应用潜力。此外，2026年以来，全球环肽领域BD交易总金额已达61.7亿美元，创历史新高。值得注意的是，该数据涵盖全球环肽交易，并非仅指口服环肽。二、HSK47388首次进入III期，早期数据已披露国内口服肽类药物研发也在持续推进。继HS-20118、HCXT-2001获得海外药企关注后，海思科的HSK47388迎来新的临床进展。HSK47388是海思科自主研发的口服、强效、高选择性IL-23抑制肽类药物，属于化学药品1类新药，研发方向包括银屑病和炎症性肠病。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此次启动的III期临床试验拟纳入390例中重度斑块状银屑病患者，采用多中心、随机、双盲设计。主要终点包括第16周PASI 90应答率，以及IGA评分达到0或1级且较基线改善至少2分的患者比例。2026年1月，海思科已公布HSK47388的I期健康受试者研究数据。截至数据披露时，研究未观察到严重不良事件，整体耐受性良好。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库药代动力学方面，该药呈线性特征，半衰期约16—18小时，初步显示每日一次给药的潜力。多次给药剂量递增研究中，受试剂量均可抑制体外IFNγ分泌。此外，增效剂型50mg的药物暴露量与未使用增效剂型的200mg剂量相当，餐前30分钟服药的食物影响有限。需要注意的是，上述数据来自健康受试者早期研究，主要反映药物安全性、药代动力学及药效学特征，尚不能直接证明其在银屑病患者中的临床疗效。此外，据摩熵医药数据库显示，海思科目前已有超过40款1类新药处于临床及后续研发阶段，研发领域涵盖呼吸系统疾病等，剂型包括片剂、吸入混悬液和吸入粉雾剂。 title: STAT Plus: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about FDA shelving fast-track review, a Canadian importer arrested, and more
content: STAT PlusNewsletterPharmalot Pharmalittle: We’re reading about FDA shelving fast-track review, a Canadian importer arrested, and more Blackstone will provide $1.5 billion to Pfizer to help develop an experimental obesity treatment Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Alex Hogan/STAT By Ed SilvermanNov. 12, 2026 Pharmalot Columnist, Senior Writer Ed Silverman[email protected]Ed’s stories explore prescription drug pricing, affordability and access, as well issues surrounding patents, litigation, and legislation. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Top of the morning to you. Gray skies are hovering over the Pharmalot campus right now, but our spirits remain sunny, nonetheless. Why? We will trot out a bit of insight from the Morning Mayor, who would say “Every new day should be unwrapped like a precious gift.” To celebrate the notion, we are brewing a fresh cuppa stimulation and invite you to join us. Remember, a prescription is not required. Our choice today is ginger peach. Meanwhile, here are a few items of interest. Hope you have a smashing day and, of course, do stay in touch. … The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has shelved the fast-track drug review initiative launched during the Trump administration by former Commissioner Marty Makary, Reuters reports. Launched in June 2025, the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher program aimed to slash drug review timelines to just one to two months ​for therapies addressing national priorities, such as urgent unmet health needs. But critics pointed to possible preferential treatment for companies meeting demands of President Trump, such as offering ‌drugs at lower prices. No new drugs have gotten a voucher since Makary’s departure, and a key component of the program — an executive council of political appointees that oversaw drug reviews ​and had a central role in speeding approvals — has gone dormant.Advertisement The U.S. Senate health committee has scheduled a pivotal vote for next week on the nomination of Heidi Overton to serve as FDA commissioner, despite lingering doubts from Republicans on the panel, STAT writes. The vote is set for Nov. 18 and, if it passes, her nomination would then go to the full Senate, where Republicans are racing to confirm nominees before Democrats take power in January. But even as he scheduled the vote, committee Chair Bill Cassidy (R-La.) remained undecided on Overton, he wrote in a post on X. It would take just one Republican on the committee to sink her nomination, assuming all Democrats vote against her. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account?
